theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Consumer Staples (+0.05%) and Financials (+0.02%) led the market today, while Consumer Discretionary (-2.10%) and Real Estate (-1.50%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.13% versus -0.00% for defensives and -0.51% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained +2.78% while the blue-chip Dow lagged at +1.19%. Small caps moved roughly in line with the broader market, with the Russell 2000 at +1.37%. The VIX fell 1.35% to 16.85, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold slipped 0.21% to $4,124.60, crude oil was little changed at $82.23, and bitcoin slipped 1.43% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
